positive_laws: Human signal outranks system ornament; people must remain specific rather than decorative tokens.
Character identity is a redundant invariant bundle, not one permanent face, portrait, hue, position, motion or material treatment.
Rich depiction increases immediacy but is not required for identity, relationship, bounded perspective or salience.
Authored human identity is more important than simulated human appearance; specificity does not require photorealism.
Character identity remains stable across Performer reassignment, representation-depth change and color loss.
Relationship can be expressed through orientation, proximity, negative space, grouping, overlap, interruption and shared-space behavior without connector diagrams.
State decorates/contextualizes identity; state must not rewrite identity.
Visible portrayal never becomes authority for belief, knowledge, observation, intention, emotion, trust or private psychology.
As visual certainty decreases, textual/programmatic identity explicitness increases while identity truth stays stable.
Image-unavailable and assistive states must preserve names, participation, perspective/opportunity reference, focus and task attribution without rebuilding a permanent portrait roster.
Transformation plus persistent perceptual invariants can preserve identity; stylistic continuity alone cannot.
Presence may act as a local law of shared space; relationship may alter available space; consequence may leave a shared field structurally non-neutral.
Cross-surface translation must inherit laws rather than copied layouts: APP may stay restrained while WEB uses greater expressive amplitude.
Theatrical absence, human priority and living consequence can survive non-cone compositions; current Stage imagery is not a universal motif.
Expressive imagery is concentrated where it earns meaning; shell/control/supporting surfaces remain capable of staying quiet and semantically complete without it.
negative_quarantine_laws: No generic profile-avatar or interchangeable AI-portrait system.
No color-only, costume-tint-only, lighting-only or fixed-headshot identity.
No gaze, expression, posture or gesture treated as authoritative psychology/state unless independently supported.
No social-graph/node language, connector beams or quantified relationship implication.
No copied cone lineup, Stage scenery, black-box theater, spotlight, floor-name or literal Stage composition as cross-surface identity shorthand.
No generic dark atmosphere, luxury editorial, cinematic fantasy concept art, mystical portal/rift or technology spectacle as identity.
No paper/collage/antiquarian archive shorthand or material metaphor outranking people.
No provider/model identity or capability spectacle outranking Character identity.
No permanent timeline, transcript wall or dashboard-card perimeter used as image/art-direction identity.
No essential task/state/identity meaning lost when expressive imagery is removed.
No historical visual source gains incumbent rights merely because it appears in this atlas.
No result-aware prompt retuning after subjective review.

controlled_comparison_facts.people: Three distinct temporary Character identities; labels and programmatic identity remain visible and are not product defaults.
controlled_comparison_facts.relationship: A and B share a current relationship; C remains a specific present participant rather than disappearing when not central.
controlled_comparison_facts.bounded_perspective: B may be the bounded perspective while C may independently carry current opportunity and A may independently hold focus; these are orthogonal state references.
controlled_comparison_facts.changed_present: An accepted causal event may reorganize the shared field; the same people remain recognizable afterward.
controlled_comparison_facts.fallback: The same facts must remain intelligible with expressive imagery removed and under monochrome/high-contrast abstraction.
controlled_comparison_facts.clr: No family may depend on F2 or F1; family boards use neutral/value-first construction until later lawful context.
